I don't personally use TikTok, but from everything I've seen secondhand, the platform appears to have become a vast repository of terrible advice. One recent video advises putting your iPhone in the freezer if it overheats…

Engadget only cites one example.

This is obviously something you shouldn't do. Doing so will very likely cause moisture to condense on the phone's internal components, either while it's in the freezer or after you take it out. Thermal shock is also a possible issue, especially since lithium batteries are particularly sensitive to that sort of thing.

The UK has been experiencing a heatwave for the past few weeks (by UK standards, at any rate), and phone repair shops are reportedly seeing a noticeable increase in cases of people bricking their devices after following such advice.

If your iPhone does overheat, Apple's own advice is to move it to a cooler environment and let it cool down naturally. Just don't leave it in a car, though. In hot weather, even the inside of a car's glove box can get hot enough to cause damage, or even start a battery fire.
